Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: wide architectural concept visualization for the Installation tab of Whale & Dolphin Orchestra, an art and bioacoustics project.
Primary request: Show a believable, beautifully restrained listening room centred on a large PHYSICAL printed world map table and small 3D-printed whale and dolphin figures, with no overhead projection. The installation should feel like a museum artwork people want to touch and listen to.
Scene/backdrop: modest contemporary gallery, warm ivory plaster walls, oak floor, soft daylight and warm gallery lights, ordinary human-scale room.
Subject: one freestanding rounded rectangular oak table approximately 2.2 metres by 1.2 metres at a height comfortable for seated and standing visitors. Thin legs with generous open space underneath. The actual tabletop is a matte cream world map, a geographically recognizable entire world with delicate muted ocean contour lines and pale sand continents. Six palm-sized ivory sculptural whale and dolphin miniatures on low round bases placed at different ocean recording sites; mix distinctive humpback whale, blunt rectangular-headed sperm whale, orca with tall dorsal fin, slender dolphin. They are clearly small tactile fabricated objects approximately 12 cm long, matte and subtly showing 3D-print layer texture, NOT live animals, NOT giant sculptures. Small muted teal, ochre, terracotta and purple rings on the bases, recording-site dots printed on the map. A slim small touchscreen at one table corner is a secondary control.
Room: six small charcoal loudspeakers distributed around the room perimeter on slim stands, a simple oak listening bench, a modest headphone hook near it. Two standing adult visitors and one seated visitor in a wheelchair with legs and wheelchair partly under the open table, naturally looking down and handling the miniatures; visitors are incidental and do not obscure the map. Keep wide clear walking space around the table. A quiet framed print with abstract sound traces on the wall may accompany it.
Style/medium: photorealistic architectural exhibition concept render, honest tactile materials, editorial exhibition photography, calm and inviting.
Composition/framing: landscape 3:2, generous wide three-quarter view from human eye level, map table is the clear focal point and whole table visible, show the open room and speakers. Credible object scale and world map.
Lighting/mood: soft daytime gallery illumination, quiet shared listening, restrained.
Constraints: no overhead projector, no ceiling camera, no immersive aquarium graphics, no glowing sci-fi map, no giant screens, no neon, no clutter, no toy-like coloured animals, no readable lettering, no logos, no watermarks. This is a proposed artwork, not documentation of a built exhibition.
